newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Kin Yat set for moderate gain on debut.
newsitem.headline: Kin Yat set for moderate gain on debut.

text.p: Shares of remote control toy car manufacturer Kin Yat Holdings Ltd are poised for moderate gains in their market debut on Thursday, analysts said on Tuesday.

"A rally on debut is expected in view of its high subscription level of over 500 times," said Ben Kwong, director of research at Dharmala Securities. "But it is hard to say how far it will surge and it will depend on market sentiment."
Analysts said recent market sentiment was a bit weak on concerns that Beijing might move to cool speculation in red chips, leading to heavy consolidation among red chips and smaller stocks.
Kin Yat offered 85 million shares at HK$1.28 each in an initial public offering (IPO) in Hong Kong. The 76.5 million shares available for public subscription were 523 times subscribed.
The grey market price of the shares is at about HK$2.20, analysts said.
"Its rally is likely to be short-lived because investors may take profit when there are no fundamentals to support the surge," one analyst at a local brokerage said.
The Hong Kong-based company manufactures toy cars and electrical household appliances.
"Concern about its reliance on a single customer, especially in the relatively volatile toy making industry, is seen making its earnings prospects less attractive," Kwong said.

Kin Yat said in its listing prospectus that sales to its largest customer, Hasbro Group, accounted for about 53 percent of turnover for the year ended in March 31, 1996, and 54 percent for the eight months to November 1996.

Kin Yat said net proceeds of HK$96.8 million would be used to acquire a new plant and machinery for two new production facilities in Shenzhen and Shaoguan, and to expand a products development project.
